what: Momentum map for the pion spectrometer online analysis. Maps a tracker channel triplet (ch0, ch1, ch2) to the momentum that produced it.
readout_note: winner-takes-all: the online decoder takes the largest amplifier, so a channel number IS an amplifier number. Channel numbering is 1-BASED; 0 means the plane did not fire.
setting_note: the two physical T1/T2 positions. One is installed for a whole run; this is NOT a per-event quantity, and the wrong setting returns confidently wrong momenta.
pattern_note: channels per ganging group, one entry per channel_widths_base value. [16, 8, 4, 7] with widths [1, 2, 4, 8] is 16 single bars, 8 pairs, 4 quads and 7 octets = 35 amplifiers.

columns.setting: which T1/T2 position this row applies to
columns.ch0: T0 channel, 1-based (0 = plane did not fire)
columns.sigma_mev: 1-sigma width of the momenta that produce this triplet
columns.ok: 1 if enough SIMULATED tracks landed on this triplet to trust sigma_mev, else 0. This is Monte-Carlo statistics from the map build, NOT detector calibration. When ok=0 the MOMENTUM is still good (its error goes as sigma/sqrt(n)); it is sigma_mev that is unreliable, and sigma_mev=0 means a single track landed here.

calibration: p_mev and sigma_mev come from a beam FLAT in momentum, so they are properties of the instrument and carry no assumption about the beam spectrum being measured.
absent_triplets: A triplet NOT in this file is one no single track can produce. Treat its absence as a veto, not as a lookup failure: it is an accidental coincidence, a hard scatter, a decay kink, or two tracks in one bunch.
